results.name: PPE compliance (helmet and vest)
results.definition: Persons observed wearing both helmet and vest / persons observed. A person = one tracked person per camera per 10-minute window (one person on two cameras counts twice).
results.baseline_window: camera-measured, pilot weeks 1-2 (11-24 May), 40 pilot cameras, per BRD v2
results.window: Average of last 4 pilot weeks (8 Jun-5 Jul), ratio of sums
results.method: Recomputed from the weekly export: sum(ppe_compliant) / sum(persons_observed), pilot cohort only
results.status: MET (91.1% vs 90%). Still above target on pilot cameras in September; all-camera figure is lower because areas added later started lower.
results.contributors: Client: safety week in April, daily toolbox talks from May, two contractor gangs suspended in May (identified from snapshots), gang bonus for >95% in Sep. Vendor: on-site retrain on 4,200 frames (15 Jun) cut false alarms so supervisors trusted the alerts.
results.worth: +22.2 points in 8 weeks on a like-for-like camera measure. The pilot areas held at ~94% three months later. It is a leading indicator; it does not by itself prove fewer injuries.

disagreements.why: 74% is the announced manual walk score (BRD says not comparable); 96.6% is the packing pilot cameras in their best week (recomputed: K1_packing_best). Client rejected this in writing.

disagreements.claim: 61% in first two weeks, 78% in week five
disagreements.why: PoC: 12 cameras, different scope and window; not the BRD baseline.

disagreements.where: BRD v2 §4; recomputed from 07_data walks file
disagreements.why: Announced walks (23 of 103 remarks say so), 2 per day, one area; BRD records it 'for reference only'.

disagreements.claim: All-camera line fell from 93.6% to about 86% in August
disagreements.why: Mix effect: added cameras start low (72% in their first week). Pilot cohort never dropped below 92%.

results.name: Restricted-zone breaches (conveyor tail pulleys, kiln hot zone)
results.definition: Entries of a tracked person's feet into a zone polygon for > 2 s, per 1,000 camera-hours of usable video, pilot cameras.
results.window: Last 4 pilot weeks; re-measured on pilot cameras for the last 4 weeks to 27 Sep
results.status: NOT MET at pilot end (−46%). Condition met by September (−77%) after the client installed physical guards on 12 Aug and the vendor added a 2 m pre-zone warning.
results.contributors: Mostly the client's physical guards (engineering control). Vendor: detection, pre-zone warning, evidence for where guards were needed.
results.worth: Report as 'missed at pilot end, then fixed together'. Do not credit software alone with −77%.

disagreements.claim: 'Restricted zone entries down by half' (1 Jul)
disagreements.why: Was −46% against a −50% target; client asked to say that.
Single week, before pilot end; BRD window is last 4 weeks.

results.name: Alert acknowledgement time
results.definition: Minutes from alert to acknowledgement by the area in-charge.
results.baseline_window: pilot weeks 1-2 (BRD says n/a; shown for context)
results.window: Last 4 pilot weeks; re-measured last 4 weeks to 27 Sep
results.method: Alert-weighted mean of weekly zone medians (the library has no alert-level data, so a true median cannot be computed). This reproduces the certificate's 4.9 and 3.5.
results.status: NOT MET at pilot end (4.9 min; the outage week inflated it). Met by September after the client's control-room phone rule (escalation live 4 Aug).
results.contributors: Client: control room phones the in-charge after 5 minutes. Vendor: alerts routed to the area in-charge, escalation hook, daily camera health message after the outage.
results.worth: Response time is what the sponsor said he was buying ('response time, not logins').

disagreements.why: Direction right; baseline is 8.6 (alert-weighted, weeks 1-2) and 2.1 is the pilot cohort in Sep; must name the phone rule as a cause.

results.name: False alarms
results.definition: Share of alerts marked false in the EHS daily sample review, scaled to the week (EHS labels, not model confidence, since 3 Jun).
results.baseline_window: pilot weeks 1-2 (BRD says n/a; PoC was 23%)
results.status: MET, narrowly (9.7%). Kiln hot-zone still above 10% at pilot end (12.1%).
results.contributors: Vendor retrain on 4,200 site frames on an on-premise box; client EHS labelled the sample.
results.worth: This is the number that kept the project alive: the Head EHS said 23% 'is how a system dies'.

results.name: Truck turnaround at the gate (added by CR-03)
results.definition: Average minutes from gate-in to gate-out per truck.
results.baseline_window: manual gate register 1 Jun-2 Aug (handwritten, rounded to 5 min, 6 days missing) - the contract baseline
results.window: Camera data 25 Aug-30 Sep (excl. 11 Sep calibration day)
finals: vs first 2 weeks of camera data (like-for-like)
results.status: MET on either basis. Quote the like-for-like −24% externally: the register baseline is not comparable.
results.contributors: Client gate-infrastructure upgrade (commissioned 18 Aug; ~6 min) and client logistics' dispatch slots run from the queue view (~16 min). Vendor: the queue view and alerts that made slots possible. The vendor itself says the split cannot be made cleanly.
results.worth: Shared credit. The gate dashboard alone (3-17 Aug) did not move turnaround much.

disagreements.why: Handwritten, rounded to 5 minutes, missing days; method changed on 3 Aug.

results.name: Money: transporter detention (the only measured money)
results.definition: Detention paid to transporters per month, from the client's ERP (finance).
results.method: From finance value note; no raw ERP data in the library
results.status: Measured, one month only. Finance credits the project with 'a share', not a number.
results.contributors: Client gate-infrastructure upgrade (own investment) and dispatch slots; vendor queue view.
results.worth: Client finance's own view: payback a little over two years if half of the detention saving is credited; under 14 months only if the full saving holds AND the insurance premium falls. Benchmark '2 crore' and '2.3 crore' figures are not used: finance rejected them. Avoided-injury savings are not claimed. Insurance is 'possible, not realised'.

disagreements.claim: 'Rs 2.3 Cr annual savings' incl. Rs 88 L avoided LTIs and Rs 30 L benchmark productivity
disagreements.why: Finance: 'We should not claim avoided LTIs as savings'; benchmark rejected at steering committee.

results.name: What the users say
results.definition: Paper survey of 18 shift supervisors run by EHS, 14-16 Sep, 1-5 scale.
results.status: Positive, with a data-quality caveat: 4 of the 18 comments repeat earlier comments word for word (rows S15-S18 copy S01-S04), so quote comments only from S01-S14 and treat the scores with care.
results.worth: Supports the user story; not a KPI.

results.name: Injuries (deliberately not claimed)
results.definition: Lost-time injuries from the EHS register.
results.status: NOT CLAIMED. Seven months at roughly one LTI per quarter is not evidence; the client (EHS and finance) said so in writing. Near-miss reports rose, but alerts became loggable as near-misses from 15 Jun, so the rise is partly a definition change.

disagreements.why: Client: 'proves nothing and the auditors will laugh at it'.

approval.reference: CS-2026-001 (anonymised case study, cement safety analytics)
approval.cc: Pooja Menon, Corporate Legal; Meenakshi Iyer, Head EHS; Rajiv Bhandari, Unit Head
approval.subject: For your review under MSA clause 15.2(e): anonymised case study draft (nothing published without your written yes)
message: As Pooja asked on 28 September, here is the complete pack for the anonymised case study about the safety-camera project: the full text, every chart and image, and a list of every number with the record it comes from. Nothing has been published or shared outside PredCo, and nothing will be without your written approval.
What we have done to protect the company:
- The company appears only as "an Indian cement manufacturer". No plant name, state, capacity, number of plants, headcount, camera count, project name or people's names.
- No photos or screenshots from site. The three images are charts and a diagram we redrew from scratch, with no addresses, logos or metadata.

- Only numbers measured the way your BRD defines them, with the targets we missed shown as missed. No injury claims, no savings estimates beyond what your finance team measured, and credit shared for what your own teams did (guards, phone rule, dispatch slots, safety week).

The one-page approval sheet gives you four choices: anonymised, named later (once you are ready and on a fresh review), internal use only, or no. You can strike any line or number, and you can withdraw approval at any time.
If it helps, we can walk Corporate Communications and Legal through it in 20 minutes on a call of your choosing.
signoff: (Pack reviewed internally before sending, per our case-study process.)
